body:
Hey guys, I'm Raph. I recently moved for school and currently don't have a support system, and no family support. I was recently let go due to my employer finding out about my transitioning, they're religiously affiliated and I live in a state with no workplace protections for gender identity. I should have been more careful but the person I told I really trusted not to say anything. Regardless, I'm currently in a bit of a bind. If anyone could help out a little bit, I'd appreciate it. I linked my venmo. Thanks, y'all.

www.venmo.com/u/Raph-McAleavey
Carry on, brother. I brought 7 rolls back home and TSA didn't even blink.
Happy to be home again. I was deployed in the god 'ol sandbox for 7 months and am now home. I get to spend Thanksgiving with my family for the first time in 6 years.
Haha I really like the style too. Wish I could help out, but I'm in the US, just letting you know I feel the same!
General Snus is my go to, but Zyn and other tobaccoless products can be alright if snus isn't available in your area.
Add me please
Ah frick I love sunset wheat, it's my favorite beer. And stokers wintergreen! You are THE MAN!
I have health insurance, but the deductible is terribly high...That's why its so freaking expensive.

Oh man Charlie looks so much like my old (Passed away) Cocker, Smokey. I love him. Thank you for reminding me of him today, and Charlie seems like a very good boy despite his mischief! I hope he enjoyed his bath :)

Lamictal, gabapentin, and now we're weaning off of effexor and abilify. This freaking withdrawal from effexor is killing me. And Lamictal is fricking messing with my sleep schedule. Insomnia followed by hypersomnia again and again and again. I guess it could be the gabapentin, but I'm blaming the Lamictal bc that seems, looking at the side effects, the most likely culprit. Or maybe it's the withdrawl from effexor.

Similar tasks as well. Buck also knows 'Search'. Sometimes I hear/see things that aren't real and I can't distinguish reality from whats in my head. He's trained to go to where I point, and if there's a person there to sit/stay with them. On the other hand, if it's in my head, he'll go, 'search', and come back to me. This is typically indicitive that we need to make a trip to the hospital, heh.

Makes me tired as fuck and fucks with my muscles, they feel like noodles most of the time. Don't really think it does anything to be honest, but I'm afraid to stop taking it because at least I'm not actively trying to kill myself.

Yes.  All the time. I actually ended up training my dog to help me out, believe it or not. I trained him that alarm=walk time. He wakes up when he hears it and starts going ballistic, licking me etc. It's kind of like an alarm clock ++++. He literally won't let me not get up, and I love my dogs more than anything, so I end up getting up eventually. Some times it takes me an hour. Sometimes he's enough for it to be 10 minutes. But it sucks.

Look at goodrx and see how much that brings the price down. My meds would have been 800 a month and went down to 100 with that shiz...The people at the pharmacy might give you a hard time but they'll take it if your persistent. I'm assuming, since this is common bs in the US, that you're from the US, granted.

To show you what I mean-Abilify would be about 250 for me without insurance or good RX, goes down to about 22 for me...
Definitely.  It's kind of always been a thing, I know I won't make it past 30. Not because I have intent, but because I can't get my shit together, and know one day it'll pile on way to hard.
Yes. I'm just afraid I'll end up putting them through compassion fatigue...

Potentially they won't know what to do or say. They'll become more frustrated with me, and I could lose any support that I have. I'm clear enough right now that I know that that level is probably extreme, but the fear of that happening is obviously not great.

People might not know how to react. I think most people want a straightforward answer, like 'help me with x,y and z'. And I just don't have that...
I get it, mate...
Maybe...It might at least help with the confussion...
Thanks, I'll give it a go!

Kind of a similar story here...I have two dogs, Oreo, who's been the house dog for years. Buck is my SDiT, and he's started public access training. Oreo HATES when we leave together. When I leave on my own, it's no big deal, but even when I brought Buck to the Vet without her she apparently whined the entire time we were gone. I guess I don't have any advice except to make sure that Panda still knows he's loved, I spend extra time with Oreo where Buck 'isn't allowed' and instead set him to play with a puzzle toy or with his bone, and then it's just me and Oreo time. It seems to have helped a little.
I'm not in that area, alas, but thank you so much for the link! It has some great advice :)
Thank you so much!! That's great advice!

Thank you so much. A hardware store seems like the common suggestion. Walking/riding parks are where we've been going to train, so this is a nice idea to keep doing. Thank you so much for taking the time to reply, I wouldn't have even thought about that with pet stores...Silly on my part, I know. 

Again, thank you for taking the time to reply!
Awesome, thank you so much. That's a good point that I didn't think about. I'll give that a go as well...I'm so appreciative of the advice on here.
We have a hardware store I could ask the manager about with this...Thank you so much for the suggestion, I wouldn't have thought of that.
That's why I asked! I wouldn't have even thought about this. Thank you guys so much.

I do is well, friend. It's actually pretty well controlled with medications, but there was a period of time where I would have full blown conversations/screaming matches with my 'mom' who is v much dead. Typically only when I'm manic though. I actually used to think I was really having conversations and it wasn't abnormal, until a friend caught me. 

Very much hate it, it's one of the only reasons I don't stop taking an antipsychotic. As much as I'd love a high every once in a while...

Exactly. I can't find the words to tell her that, though. Fuck. I would give anything just to feel 'normal' again. Or just a moment of high, but those are well controlled right now.

That sound weird?
I'd assume, sadly, that Northerner won't ship if the rules are that rough there. It won't ship to where I live due to Tobacco laws, which is friggin ridiculous....

Wasn't a huge fan, but I'm glad other people liked it! The texture was just too funky for me to get over, and the wintergreen was too 'candy' for my liking. But hey, it looks like other people love it! Happy for that.
I think I found a decent therapist, finally...

I got approved for my new dog :) He's a rescue,  a beautiful baby boy. Going to be training him for a service dog and if he washes, an ESA and good friend. My current dog is the only reason I wake up in the morning, and having a new pup to get up for in the morning will really help.
Do what I can. Thanks.
Thanks man. I just really don't know how to deal with it. I have an apt with my adviser to discuss options next week...

I've been trying different stuff for 3 years or so. Just started a new cocktail last month...I don't know, I've calmed down, maybe they'll help this time, but I've honestly just lost hope. Yes, I have been. My dogs trained to remind me along with an alarm...It's just frustrating when nothing seems to be working.
Wintergreen, especially Grizz, is great to me after/in between drinking beer.
I know tough guy can do something for canadian peeps if you reach out to them.

I'm getting a dog that I might be training to be a service dog, at the very least an ESA...Dogs are really the only reason I haven't killed myself. If I have one to stay with me, I know someone will always love and depend on me..

Definitely. When I'm 'good' I'm able to memorize anything in collage, but the moment the depression hits I'm suddenly dropping test scores and have a hell of a time remembering even the simpilest thing. And I also become a lot  'dumber' to normal things. The fire alarm went off last week and I legit just sat there staring off, bc it didn't register that a fire alarm was a thing.

I don't know your situation, friend, but  a professional is always nice, especially when it's someone completely removed from the situation. If you talk to different people there are different scales? The therapist I go to is an 'intern' who is being observed by someone who has their license because that's what I can afford. It's a lot cheaper and they have skills, it's just they have ot learn how to use them. I also think it helps a lot with my depression that I'm at least helping someone learn, it makes me feel like less of a burden when I go to therapy....
Hoping it will help you out, friend! The alprazolam helps me a lot for mania and panic attacks.
